_comment: SYNTHETIC plain-language knowledge base for the RAG retrieval layer. Each document is a pre-approved, non-diagnostic snippet. Retrieved snippets are grounding for the explanation draft; they never change the tier the rule engine assigned. Medical-director sign-off (per Q3) is simulated by the 'approved' flag.

documents.text: Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body. It is one of the most common things a blood test measures.
A hemoglobin value below the usual range is often described as a low result. Low hemoglobin is a common finding and a doctor looks at it alongside your history to understand it.
Fasting glucose is the amount of sugar in your blood after not eating for several hours. It is a routine check related to how your body handles sugar.

A fasting glucose above the usual range means the sugar level was higher than typical on this sample. A single reading is only a snapshot and is usually repeated or confirmed before any conclusions are drawn.
HbA1c reflects your average blood sugar over roughly the past three months, rather than a single moment. It is commonly tracked over time.
Cholesterol is a fatty substance in your blood. A lipid profile looks at total cholesterol along with LDL, HDL and triglycerides to give a fuller picture.
LDL is sometimes called the less favourable type of cholesterol. A higher LDL is something a cardiologist or physician commonly reviews as part of overall heart-health planning.
TSH is a hormone that helps regulate your thyroid gland. Thyroid results are interpreted together and often rechecked over time by an endocrinologist.
Creatinine is a waste product that healthy kidneys filter out of the blood. It is a common marker of how the kidneys are working and is read alongside age and other values.
Potassium is an electrolyte that helps your heart and muscles work. Both very high and very low potassium are treated as urgent because of their effect on the heart.
A potassium level far outside the safe range is treated as a time-sensitive finding that a clinician needs to review right away.
Sodium is an electrolyte that helps balance fluid in the body. Large shifts in sodium are reviewed promptly by a clinician.
Troponin is a protein released when the heart muscle is under strain. A raised troponin is always treated as urgent and reviewed by a clinician immediately.
Vitamin D supports bone health. A lower-than-usual vitamin D is a very common and generally manageable finding that your physician can advise on.
One lab value is a single snapshot. Doctors read it together with your symptoms, history and other results before deciding what it means for you.
A reference range is the band of values seen in most healthy people of your age and sex. Being just outside it is common and is not the same as a diagnosis.
